note: Attacker-controlled raw input bytes are passed to libbpf's object parser, which will parse the ELF structure and locate the .BTF.ext section.
The .BTF.ext section data is passed to btf_ext__new, which creates a btf_ext structure pointing to the raw section data.
The btf_ext header is parsed, validating magic, version, and hdr_len. The attacker controls hdr_len to be a valid value <= data_size.
btf_ext_setup_info is called for func_info with attacker-controlled off and len values from the header.
The info pointer is computed as data + hdr_len + off. The expression hdr_len + off is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic and can overflow, wrapping to a small value.
info_left is set to the attacker-controlled len value, which remains large even though info points to a small offset due to the 32-bit overflow.

The bounds check compares data + data_size against info + len. Due to the 32-bit overflow in hdr_len + off, info points to a small offset, so info + len may pass the check even though the actual data region is smaller.
The record_size is read from the attacker-controlled data at the wrapped info pointer. This value is used to compute total_record_size.
num_records is read from attacker-controlled data. The attacker sets num_records to a large value to cause the loop to iterate many times.
total_record_size is computed as sec_hdrlen + num_records * record_size. The attacker controls both num_records and record_size to make total_record_size small enough to pass the info_left check.
The check passes because total_record_size is small due to attacker-controlled values, allowing the loop to proceed.
sinfo points to the first btf_ext_info_sec structure within the wrapped info region.

The while loop reads sinfo->num_info and other fields. Due to the 32-bit overflow in hdr_len + off, the loop iterates over attacker-controlled data that extends beyond the actual .BTF.ext section bounds, causing an UNKNOWN READ when accessing memory outside the allocated buffer.

sinfo advances by total_record_size each iteration. The attacker controls total_record_size to be small, causing many iterations that eventually read past the end of the buffer, triggering the UNKNOWN READ crash.
